title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatises a 'contexte' C, read here as a tame-topology framework in the spirit of Esquisse §5. It consists of a set 𝓕 of 'figures' with a least element ∅_𝓕 and several relations:
- ≤ : 'is a subfigure of' (inclusion);
- ≲ : 'is a subdivision of'. The previous page states axiom C8 on gluing subdivisions and shows Subdiv(∐F_i) ≅ ∏ Subdiv(F_i).
- ≪ : defined by F' ≪ F iff F' ≤ F̄ for some subdivision F̄ ≲ F. So F' is a subfigure of some subdivision of F, i.e. F' 'lies in' F up to refinement.
There is also a distinguished subclass 𝓜 of figures (cell-like or 'irreducible' figures). The next page writes X ∈ 𝒰 with X ≤ F.

Crossed-out first attempt (end of p.86 and top of this page). He tried to prove that, for F ≠ ∅, two minimality conditions are equivalent:
- (a) F is minimal for ≤;
- (b) F is minimal for ≪.
The direction b ⇒ a is trivial, since ≤ implies ≪ (take F̄ = F). For a ⇒ b: given F' ≪ F, i.e. F' ≤ F̄ ≲ F, he wants F̄ = F, so that F' ≤ F and hence F' = F. The step 'a ≤-minimal figure admits only the trivial subdivision' needs an axiom (he tries C7, then strikes it out). He abandons the proof ('On va le prouver d'abord').

What he does instead. He takes (b) as the definition. A 'lieu' (place, point) of C is a nonzero figure minimal for ≪: F ≠ ∅_𝓕, and F' ≪ F with F' ≠ ∅_𝓕 implies F' = F. He then remarks:
- a lieu lies in 𝓜 and is ≤-minimal there;
- the converse is NOT derivable from the axioms so far, but will hold in the good ('bons'?) contexts.

New definitions.
- 𝓛 is the set of lieux. This is how the 'points' are recovered from a point-free calculus of figures.
- The shadow ('ombre') of a figure is |F| = {x ∈ 𝓛 : x ≪ F}. This is the underlying point set, invariant under subdivision.
- The multishadow ('multiombre') is the family F̂ = {|X| : X ∈ 𝓜, X ≤ F} of shadows of the cells of F (continued on p.88).

On p.88 he proves |F| = ∪|X|; this uses an earlier proposition (p.78): a point under F lies under a smallest cell X ≤ F. He then proves that the multishadow is an 'admissible' family of subsets of 𝓛:
- every member A has nonempty 'open cell' A° = A \ δA, where δA is the union of the proper members contained in A;
- the intersection of two members is a union of members.
This is the point-set combinatorial shadow of a regular cell/polyhedral complex.

Purpose: recover from the axiomatic calculus of figures and subdivisions an underlying set of points, together with a stratified cell decomposition, as a step toward 'tame topology'.
errors: The transcribed sentence 'comme ≪ implique ≤' gets the logic backwards. What holds by definition is that ≤ implies ≪ (take F̄ = F). The ink is ambiguous and this deduction is crossed out, so this is either a slip of the manuscript or of the transcription.

In the abandoned proof of a ⇒ b, the step 'F̄ = F' (a ≤-minimal figure has only trivial subdivisions) is unjustified by the axioms in force. Grothendieck himself recognises the gap, abandons the proof and makes ≪-minimality the definition. He states explicitly that the converse is not provable 'dans l'état actuel des choses'.

ideas.what: Relation F' ≪ F: F' is a subfigure of some subdivision of F (containment up to refinement).
ideas.modern_name: Containment of polyhedra/cells up to subdivision (PL or o-minimal cell decompositions); refinement preorder
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this axiomatics unpublished

ideas.what: Points ('lieux') defined as nonzero figures minimal for ≪, i.e. recovering points from a point-free calculus of figures and subdivisions.
ideas.modern_name: Points as minimal nonzero elements / atoms of a refinement order (cf. pointless topology, atoms of a lattice)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pointless topology tradition (Stone, Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone); not in this subdivision-based form

ideas.what: Shadow |F| = set of points ≪ F, and multishadow = family of shadows of the cells of F.
ideas.modern_name: Underlying point set (realization) of a figure, plus the induced cell/face decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in cell-complex theory in concrete settings

ideas.what: Admissible families of subsets: every member has nonempty open cell A \ δA, and intersections are unions of members.
ideas.modern_name: Regular cell complex / stratification axioms in set-theoretic form (face-poset combinatorics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cell-complex combinatorics (Björner et al.), stratified spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates a precise open question in his axiomatic tame-topology framework: whether every ≤-minimal cell (an element of 𝓜 minimal for ≤) is a lieu (≪-minimal). He notes it fails under the axioms so far and expects it in 'good' contexts, without stating which axiom guarantees it. A minimal axiom forcing 'minimal cells admit no nontrivial subdivision' was never formulated in print.
missed.quote: mais il n'est pas vrai, dans l'état actuel des choses, i.e. avec les axiomes ... introduits jusqu'à présent, que l'inverse soit vrai
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Axiomatising tame topology without a prior point set (e.g. o-minimal or PL structures recovered from a calculus of figures and subdivisions) is still not done systematically. This is a concrete criterion for when points can be recovered.

missed.claim: Points are recovered as atoms of a 'contained-up-to-subdivision' preorder on figures, and a regular cell complex is recovered as the 'multiombre'. This links Grothendieck's tame topology to point-free topology / locale theory and to the definable-set theory of o-minimality. The later literature did not make this link explicit.
missed.quote: On appelle lieu de C un élément de F∖{∅_F} minimal pour ≪ ... on appelle ombre de F l'ens. des x ∈ L tels que x ≪ F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a point-free, subdivision-invariant foundation for tame geometry. Such a foundation could be compared with o-minimal 'definable spaces' and with Hrushovski–Loeser-type constructions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is part of the unpublished, detailed axiomatics behind the tame topology programme of Esquisse §5, which is notable as a record. The specific content, however, is definitional (points as ≪-minimal figures, shadows, multishadows) and fairly natural once the framework exists. Its main interest is as evidence of a point-free approach to tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'Ainsi, on voit qu'un lieu est minimal [?] ∈ 𝓜' probably reads 'Ainsi, on voit qu'un lieu est un élément ∈ 𝓜' (or similar). The point is that a lieu belongs to 𝓜.
The parenthetical at the end of the lieu discussion reads roughly '(Ce sera vrai cependant pour les "contextes ... bons"?)'. The adjective is uncertain (possibly 'bons' or 'bornés').
Before 'en résulte' the image reads 'comme ≪ (implique) ≤' with insertion marks. Logically it should be '≤ implique ≪'.
On the next page, 'La multiplication [?]' should read 'La multiombre'.
In 'Ceci dit ... il en résulte que', the first word is 'Ceci dit' (as transcribed). The struck words before the earlier line read 'Mais si'.
